learning: Ask the simulator whether the outer sensors saturate at ±0.03 m, whether kp 2.5 causes oscillation, and whether base_speed 1.4 still completes the course within 3 s.
notes: Integrated the Builder's ±0.03 m, y = 0.02 m array with a retuned controller: kp raised to 2.5 for the lower signal gain, kd lowered to 0.12 for the shorter lookahead, and base_speed reduced to 1.4 to favour finishing. Symmetric weights and last_direction line loss are kept.
rationale: The Builder's proposal widens the array to x = ±0.03 m at 15 mm spacing and moves the row to y = 0.02 m. The baseline evidence is all off-track ends at max_error about 0.06 m, with 1 to 2 line-loss events per run, 0.07 to 0.16 steering oscillation, and progress of 0.10 to 0.19. Two effects follow from the new geometry. First, the outer sensors sit further out, so the signal per metre of offset is lower: a weight of ±2 at ±0.03 m gives about 67 weight per metre against about 100 in the baseline. I raise kp from 2.0 to 2.5 to restore roughly the baseline steering gain. Second, the shorter lookahead reduces lag, so the derivative term can drop from 0.15 to 0.12 without losing damping. I keep the symmetric weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] so the signal sign convention matches the contract (positive x is left, positive signal steers left). I lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.4. The robot has been leaving the tape early on every track, so a finish is worth more than a slightly faster time, and completion time costs at most 60 points out of 3 s. The 1.4 setting still needs about 1.3 m/s or more to finish within 3 s, so it is a trade-off to check in the race. ki stays at 0.05 and last_direction stays as the line-loss rule, because it recovered from short losses in the baseline without a catastrophic failure. Expected result is a stronger steering response that holds the tape under the wider array, with fewer line losses and lower oscillation. This is an expectation and has not been measured.
